## 📰 News

- **2026-09-05 — dshrc 0.1.0.** First release: pair a phone with a short-lived code,
start and drive

`dsh` sessions over ACP, approve tool calls with one tap, receive
self-hosted push notifications, a

nd reach the daemon over LAN, Tailscale, or an
outbound relay. A terminal client and an Even Realiti

es G2 glasses client are
included. Full notes in the Changelog.

## How it works

dshrc spawns `deepseek-acp` directly over
stdio — no subcommand or mode flags, since any argv it doe

sn't recognize as
`--setup`/`--version`/`--help` falls through to running as an ACP service. The dae

mon,
ACP client, pairing, push, relay, and phone/PWA/glasses clients all speak the same typed
protoc

ol regardless of which agent is on the other end of the pipe, so the whole stack
above the transport
layer never has to know or care that the agent is `deepseek-acp`.
A few things worth knowing about how this backend behaves:

- **Model selection** goes through the `DEEPSEEK_ACP_MODEL` environment variable —
`deepseek-acp` ha

s no `--model` CLI flag of its own.
- **Approvals are structurally guaranteed.** `deepseek-acp`'s sa

ndbox always sends
`session/request_permission` before a tool leaves the session's working directory

—
there is no config key, flag, or environment variable that turns it off. There is no
state a phon

e-controlled session can end up in where tools run unattended without the
phone getting a say. See S

ECURITY.md.
- **One process per session.** Every spawned session is its own `deepseek-acp`
process —

there is no shared-backend mode to configure. (`--leader` is accepted in
config files for compatibi

is no shared-backend mode to configure. (`--leader` is accepted in
config files for compatibility.)
## 🔭 What's next

The roadmap builds on dsh's own session store. Verified against real files: dsh
writes one compresse

d `session.jsonl.zstd` per session under `$DSH_HOME/sessions/` and
keeps no live-process registry. T
hree features build on that store, in order:

- **Session discovery** — list sessions started outside dshrc, from the store itself.
The reader dec

ompresses the zstd JSONL and reads the `type:"session"` header line and
the later `session/title` ev

ent; the schema is documented in code comments in
`src/daemon/session-manager.ts`.
- **Registry-chec

ked take-over** — reclaim a session another process has open, with a
"refuse to join a standalone ow

ner" guard. `takeOver()` resumes today; the guard
builds on a live-process registry to check against

.
- **Observed mode** — mirror a session started by hand elsewhere, by tailing its
compressed log wi
th the same reader (`src/daemon/observer.ts`).

Session **resume of a session dshrc itself created** works today — `deepseek-acp` advertises
ACP's `

loadSession` capability, and the on-disk existence check matches dsh's real
directory-naming scheme.
PRs on any of the three are very welcome.
## 🔒 Security in one line

Remote control of a coding agent **is** remote code execution. Pair devices, prefer Tailscale
or rel

ay over open LAN — approvals need no extra configuration; the sandbox always asks.
See SECURITY.md.
